mechanism_narrative: A persistently low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS below 0.5%) indicates accommodative monetary policy that compresses equity discount rates, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS remains below 0.5% for 3 consecutive months but S&P 500 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of such periods.

mechanism_narrative: When unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeds 6.0% for two consecutive months, it signals labor market deterioration that reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods where UNRATE > 6.0% for 2 consecutive months, S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in real GDP growth (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) indicates broad-based economic weakness that reduces corporate revenue expectations, predicting negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint decline in GDPC1 and HOUST fails to predict negative returns, with Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During post-pandemic recovery periods, a year-over-year CPIAUCSL increase above 2.5% signals inflationary pressures that prompt Federal Reserve tightening, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: In post-pandemic recovery periods, CPIAUCSL > 2.5% YoY fails to predict negative returns, with 5-day forward returns positive in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) above 100,000 signals labor market strength that boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: PAYEMS growth above 100,000 fails to predict positive returns, with Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) falls below 95.0 (index, 2017=100) for two consecutive months, it indicates manufacturing contraction that reduces corporate output and profits, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods where INDPRO < 95.0 for 2 consecutive months, S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in retail sales (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) indicates weakening consumer demand and housing market contraction, predicting negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to reduced revenue growth expectations.
failure_condition: The joint decline in RSAFS and HOUST fails to predict negative returns, with Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During supply chain disruption periods (INDPRO < 95.0 for 3 consecutive months), a current INDPRO level below 95.0 signals persistent supply constraints that reduce corporate output and profitability, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In supply chain disruption periods (INDPRO < 95.0 for 3 consecutive months), S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of cases.
